## Natural history notes

A slender, stick-like grasshopper characterized by its long narrow body, pointed head, short wings, and green to brown coloration that helps it blend into cattails, grasses, and rushes. In Florida, it is found in marshes, pond edges, ditches, wet prairies, canals, and other freshwater wetlands with tall emergent vegetation. It feeds mainly on grasses, cattails, sedges, and related wetland plants, usually clinging lengthwise to stems where its shape and coloration provide camouflage from predators.
